Noah (sales): Quick prep for NovaEdge POC kickoff tomorrow. They have four asks: (1) peering vs PrivateLink recommendation, (2) how to guarantee a single egress IP for their firewall, (3) short port/SG list we can paste into procurement, (4) whether SNI / client IP survive and any signed-header option for forensics. Need paste-ready bullets.

Priya (netops): Super short: peering preserves client TCP src IP end-to-end. PrivateLink creates ENIs in customer VPC so traffic toward our connector appears from those ENI IPs (network-level src will be ENI).

Arun (eng): For HTTP(S) we can emit a signed header carrying original client info: `X-Redwood-Client: <base64(sig>|ip|ts|id)` that the customer can verify (HMAC with shared secret). This gives stronger provenance than plain X-Forwarded-For. For opaque TLS streams (non-HTTP) you wont get that without peering or an in-VPC proxy that terminates and re-injects metadata.

Marta (security): Signed header option: requires a pre-shared verification key on customer's side (we can rotate). Note: signed-header + timestamp reduces spoofing risk but doesn't replace cryptographic client auth. If they need cryptographic proof of source device, advise mutual-TLS from client to their ingress or peering + client cert mapping.

Priya (netops): Minimal SG / firewall bullets to paste: 
- Allow outbound TCP/443 from your router/subnet to our control plane CIDR (we'll provide exact list at handshake).
- If using PrivateLink: allow inbound TCP/443 from connector ENI CIDRs (provided at setup).
- If peering: allow TCP/443 across peering and update route tables accordingly.
- Allow outbound UDP/123 to NTP or require reachable time service.

Noah (sales): They also asked: "Can Redwood guarantee a single static egress IP we can whitelist?"

Priya (netops): Yes — the pattern is to NAT connector egress through a NAT Gateway/EIP or a Transit EIP in the customer's account. We cannot provide an IP inside their VPC; they control the NAT. If they want a cloud-provider-managed HA NAT, recommend AWS NAT Gateway with Elastic IP or a small proxy fleet fronting connector egress.

Arun (eng): Performance note for the POC: if they plan sustained >200MB/s or large parallel streams, peering + TGW + dedicated connector subnet reduces fragmentation/MTU issues. For PrivateLink, ENI limits and cross-AZ bandwidth can matter.

Marta (security): SNI visibility: SNI is visible in ClientHello unless clients use ESNI. If their IDS/TLS-inspector does TLS termination, they must preserve signed headers or reattach them after re-encryption. Document paste: "SNI: visible to pass-through devices; TLS interception must be architected to preserve auth headers."

Arun (eng): Egress cost ballpark for POC: if they expect ~10TB/month, estimate cloud egress ~$0.09/GB (varies by region/provider) -> ~$900/month in egress data transfer plus Private deploy infra fee. We should caveat: exact pricing depends on region and sustained commit; we can produce a formal quote once they give expected tokens/sec and average response sizes.

handoff-bot: Handshake ticket created: https://redwood.internal/handshakes/NE-9007  netops to attach ENI ranges, sample SG, and HMAC key exchange instructions.

Noah (sales): Awesome. Can someone paste-ready two lines for procurement SOC re: logs and keys?

Marta (security): Paste-ready: "Logs: request metadata and operational logs are retained per customer-configured retention in the Private deploy control plane; payload content is not retained unless customer enables audit logging. Keys: supports customer-managed KMS/HSM; we can integrate with cloud KMS or provide customer-supplied HSM integration."

Priya (netops): I'll add the exact connector ENI CIDR ranges and a reference SG + NAT/EIP pattern into the handshake ticket by EOD.

Arun (eng): I'll attach a short note on the signed-header HMAC format and sample verification code snippet for their app team.

Noah (sales): Perfect  I'll send the bullets to NovaEdge and confirm peering vs PrivateLink decision on tomorrow's call. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
